skill.name: api-documenter
skill.description: Create and improve API documentation using OpenAPI 3.1, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schemas, SDK examples, developer portals, and documentation testing workflows.
skill.summary: Build accurate API docs, specs, examples, portals, and migration guidance.
skill.author: sickn33

content.value_statement: API teams lose time when specs, examples, and portals drift from real behavior. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through accurate, maintainable API documentation.
actual_capabilities: Author OpenAPI 3.1 and AsyncAPI specifications with examples and auth flows.
Plan developer portal navigation, onboarding, and search structure.
Generate SDK and code example documentation across common languages.
Design migration guides, changelogs, and versioned API docs.
Define validation workflows for specs, snippets, and documentation tests.
limitations: Does not run tools or publish documentation unless the host agent has those capabilities.
Requires accurate API behavior, source specs, or repository context from the user.
Cannot verify live endpoint behavior without access to tests or API environments.
May need domain review for legal, security, or regulated API wording.

use_cases.title: Write Launch-Ready API Docs
use_cases.description: Create endpoint guides, auth explanations, examples, and error references before a new API release.

use_cases.title: Standardize API Specifications
use_cases.description: Turn inconsistent endpoint notes into OpenAPI or AsyncAPI specifications with schemas and examples.

use_cases.title: Improve Developer Onboarding
use_cases.description: Design portal structure, SDK docs, and migration paths that help developers integrate faster.

prompt_templates.title: Document One Endpoint
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-documenter to write clear documentation for this endpoint. Include purpose, parameters, authentication, responses, errors, and one example request.

prompt_templates.title: Create an OpenAPI Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-documenter to review this API surface and propose an OpenAPI 3.1 documentation plan. Identify missing schemas, examples, and auth flows.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Developer Portal Outline
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-documenter to design a developer portal for these APIs. Include navigation, onboarding path, search needs, SDK docs, and maintenance workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit and Modernize API Docs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use api-documenter to audit this documentation set for developer experience, accuracy, versioning, testing, and migration needs. Prioritize fixes with rationale.

output_examples.input: A REST API has incomplete authentication docs and scattered endpoint notes.
output_examples.output: A documentation plan covering OAuth flows, token refresh guidance, endpoint groups, response examples, error handling, and review checkpoints.

output_examples.input: A team needs a migration guide for a breaking API version change.
output_examples.output: A migration outline with audience segments, breaking change summaries, upgrade steps, compatibility notes, testing guidance, and rollout messaging.

output_examples.input: A developer portal lacks onboarding and search structure.
output_examples.output: A portal map with quickstart flow, authentication path, SDK sections, troubleshooting pages, feedback loops, analytics needs, and maintenance ownership.

best_practices: Provide real API behavior, authentication rules, and example payloads before asking for final documentation.
Ask for validation steps so specs, snippets, and guides stay aligned with implementation.
Review generated docs with product, engineering, security, and support stakeholders before publication.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to invent endpoint behavior without source material or clear assumptions.
Do not publish generated security guidance without review from qualified owners.
Do not treat documentation generation as a replacement for API contract testing.

faq.question: Can this skill create OpenAPI specifications?
faq.answer: Yes. It can guide OpenAPI 3.1 specification authoring with schemas, examples, authentication flows, and validation planning.

faq.question: Does it support AsyncAPI and GraphQL documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill covers AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema documentation, webhooks, and event-driven API documentation patterns.

faq.question: Can it generate SDK documentation?
faq.answer: Yes. It can plan SDK docs, usage examples, package distribution notes, and generated client library guidance.

faq.question: Can it verify that an API works?
faq.answer: Only when the host agent has access to tests, specs, or API environments. Otherwise it can define verification steps.

faq.question: Is this useful for developer portals?
faq.answer: Yes. It can design portal navigation, onboarding flows, API explorers, search structure, and maintenance workflows.

faq.question: Which assistants can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
